title: Money & currency
body:
Japan's currency is the yen (¥); reference rate {{fact:fx-rate-usd-jpy}}. Carry more cash than a Tokyo trip would need — Misasa Onsen ryokan, the Kurayoshi bus, and Kabuyu public bath are all cash-friendlier than card-friendly.

⚠ 7-Eleven ATMs are the commonly cited option for foreign cards in Japan, but that guidance here rests on a search summary rather than a direct fetch of the source — confirm your specific card network works before relying on it, especially once you're away from a 7-Eleven in Kurayoshi or Misasa.

title: Budget & daily costs
intro: Per-person estimates for the Oct 20–23 window. Lodging and food skew toward a ryokan-style stay in Misasa Onsen (dinner + breakfast typically included in the room rate there, so treat the two lines together rather than adding them twice for those nights).

items.label: Lodging, per night (Misasa Onsen ryokan, 2 meals included)
items.note: Range from public Misasa Onsen ryokan listings — not fetched from a single primary source and not yet booked; confirm at booking.

Local transport, per day (San'in Line, Hinomaru Bus, occasional taxi)
Sights & activities, per day (Sand Museum, Uradome cruise, Nageiredo climb, Kabuyu)
items.note: Averaged across the trip — the Nageiredo climb day runs above this on its own (¥1,200 with the climb, ¥400 without it). The Uradome cruise (¥1,800) is not on the four-day plan; add it only if you swap out a morning.
